title: Represented-scheme Zariski and etale module extension, restriction and unit
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $T$ a scheme over $S$. Regard $T$ as its represented algebraic space $h_T$ [def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space], with the small etale ringed site of [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] with section modules in the same universe as the scheme rings, without equating that universe to the larger object universe of the presented site. The functor $i_T:T_{\mathrm{et}}\to(h_T)_{\mathrm{et}}$ from the ordinary small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] sends $v:V\to T$ to its Yoneda chart $h_V\to h_T$ and sends a morphism to its Yoneda map. It is continuous and preserves the section rings of regular functions. Define $I_T$ to be restriction of module sheaves along $i_T$ with this identity ring map; it is an equivalence of the two presentations of the small etale module category. On the ordinary scheme site use the ring, Zariski restriction, tensor extension and proof-only context of [def-sfb-scheme-zariski-etale-module-constructions]. Let $c_T$ be the canonical proof context asserting continuity of the open-subscheme inclusion and existence of the tensor left adjoint to restriction; it supplies no additional module, ring, functor or map. Write $r_T$ and $e_T$ for its specified restriction and tensor extension. Define $R_T=r_T\circ I_T$ (first $I_T$, then $r_T$), and $E_T=I_T^{-1}\circ e_T$ (first $e_T$, then $I_T^{-1}$). Thus $R_T:\operatorname{Mod}((h_T)_{\mathrm{et}},\mathcal O)\to\operatorname{Mod}(T_{\mathrm{Zar}},\mathcal O_T)$ is actual restriction to open subschemes and $E_T$ is its canonical ringed-site tensor extension. Equip $E_T\dashv R_T$ with the composite of the ordinary tensor-extension/restriction adjunction and the inverse equivalence adjunction of $I_T$. Its unit and counit are those of this composite, not arbitrary natural maps. In tensor coordinates the unit inserts $1\otimes m$; for a general Zariski module the extension is sheafified tensor pullback. For a quasi-coherent module no sheafification is needed in the usual tensor-section description. No quasi-coherence, quasi-compactness, nonemptiness, or nonzero-ring assumption is imposed in defining these functors and their adjunction.
